source: Hand-tuned for gameplay; altitudes/periods are real orbital values, other columns are simplified

rows: Close to Earth: cheap to reach, great for sharp pictures, but air drag pulls you down within a couple of years.
Passes over every place on Earth at the same local time each day. The favorite orbit for Earth-observing satellites.
Hovers over one spot on the equator. Always in contact and always sees the same half of Earth, but it's far away.
Circling the Moon. Needs a big engine burn to get captured, and Earth is 384,000 km away for your radio.
Circling Mars, 225 million km from home on average. Getting captured takes a big burn, and your radio has a very long way to shout.
